require "axlsx"
require "fileutils"

# Service for exporting Customer data to Excel format
# Inherits from the base Excel export service
module Export
  class OrderExportService < ExcelExportService::Base
    # @param orders [ActiveRecord::Relation] collection of orders to export
    # @param options [Hash] additional options for customizing the export
    def initialize(orders, options = {})
      @orders = orders
      @options = options
    end

    # Generate Excel data as binary stream
    # @return [String] binary Excel data
    def generate
      package = Axlsx::Package.new
      workbook = package.workbook

      workbook.add_worksheet(name: worksheet_name) do |sheet|
        # Add styles
        styles = define_styles(workbook)

        # Add headers
        sheet.add_row headers, style: styles[:header]

        # Add data rows
        @orders.each do |order|
          data = row_data(order)
          # Format NIK and SIM CARD as text to prevent scientific notation
          sheet.add_row data, style: [
            styles[:data], # ID PESANAN
            styles[:data], # PELANGGAN
            styles[:text], # NIK - force text format
            styles[:data], # PRODUCT NAME
            styles[:data], # SMB NAME
            styles[:data], # SALES
            styles[:text], # SIM CARD - force text format
            styles[:data], # HARGA TOTAL
            styles[:data], # DEPOSIT JAMINAN
            styles[:data], # STATUS
            styles[:data], # DOKUMEN
            styles[:data]  # DIBUAT PADA
          ]
        end

        # Auto-fit columns
        sheet.column_widths(*column_widths)
      end

      package.to_stream.read
    end

    # Generate and save Excel file to disk
    # @param filepath [String] path where the file should be saved
    # @return [String] path to the generated file
    def generate_file(filepath)
      # Ensure the directory exists
      FileUtils.mkdir_p(File.dirname(filepath))

      # Generate the Excel data
      package = Axlsx::Package.new
      workbook = package.workbook

      workbook.add_worksheet(name: worksheet_name) do |sheet|
        # Add styles
        styles = define_styles(workbook)

        # Add headers
        sheet.add_row headers, style: styles[:header]

        # Add data rows
        @orders.each do |order|
          data = row_data(order)
          # Format NIK and SIM CARD as text to prevent scientific notation
          sheet.add_row data, style: [
            styles[:data], # ID PESANAN
            styles[:data], # PELANGGAN
            styles[:text], # NIK - force text format
            styles[:data], # PRODUCT NAME
            styles[:data], # SMB NAME
            styles[:data], # SALES
            styles[:text], # SIM CARD - force text format
            styles[:data], # HARGA TOTAL
            styles[:data], # DEPOSIT JAMINAN
            styles[:data], # STATUS
            styles[:data], # DOKUMEN
            styles[:data]  # DIBUAT PADA
          ]
        end

        # Auto-fit columns
        sheet.column_widths(*column_widths)
      end

      # Serialize directly to the file
      package.serialize(filepath)

      # Return the path for convenience
      filepath
    end

    private

    # Worksheet name
    # @return [String] name of the worksheet
    def worksheet_name
      "Orders"
    end

    # Excel column headers
    # @return [Array<String>] array of column headers
    def headers
      [
        "ID PESANAN",
        "PELANGGAN",
        "NIK",
        "PRODUCT NAME",
        "SMB NAME",
        "SALES",
        "SIM CARD",
        "HARGA TOTAL PER BULAN TERMASUK PPN",
        "DEPOSIT JAMINAN",
        "STATUS",
        "DOKUMEN",
        "DIBUAT PADA"
      ]
    end

    # Order data for a row
    # @param order [Order] the order to get data for
    # @return [Array] data for the row
    def row_data(order)
      # Get first postpaid activation for SIM card data
      first_activation = order.postpaid_activations.first

      # Get document status summary
      total_docs = DocumentApproval::DOCUMENT_TYPES.size
      uploaded_docs = DocumentApproval::DOCUMENT_TYPES.count { |doc| order.send(doc).attached? }
      approved_docs = DocumentApproval::DOCUMENT_TYPES.count { |doc| order.document_approved?(doc) }
      rejected_docs = DocumentApproval::DOCUMENT_TYPES.count { |doc| order.document_rejected?(doc) }
      pending_docs = uploaded_docs - approved_docs - rejected_docs

      document_status = "#{approved_docs} Approved, #{pending_docs} Pending, #{rejected_docs} Rejected (#{uploaded_docs}/#{total_docs} Uploaded)"

      [
        order.order_reference_number,
        order.customer&.company_name || order.regular_user_name,
        safe_customer_nik(order),
        order.first_order_item_product_name,
        order.customer&.company_name,
        order.sales_name,
        safe_msisdn_number(first_activation),
        order.total_price_with_vat,
        order.security_deposit_with_vat,
        order.status&.humanize,
        document_status,
        order.created_at&.strftime("%d %B %Y, %H:%M")
      ]
    end

    # Column widths for auto-fitting
    # @return [Array<Integer>] array of column widths
    def column_widths
      headers.map { |header| header.length + 10 }
    end

    # Define styles for the worksheet
    # @param workbook [Axlsx::Workbook] workbook to add styles to
    # @return [Hash] hash of styles
    def define_styles(workbook)
      {
        header: workbook.styles.add_style(
          bg_color: "000000",
          fg_color: "FFFFFF",
          b: true,
          alignment: { horizontal: :center }
        ),
        data: workbook.styles.add_style(
          alignment: { horizontal: :left }
        ),
        text: workbook.styles.add_style(
          alignment: { horizontal: :left },
          format_code: "@"
        )
      }
    end

    private

    # Safely get customer NIK, handling decryption errors gracefully
    # @param order [Order] the order to get NIK from
    # @return [String] NIK or "N/A" if not available or decryption fails
    def safe_customer_nik(order)
      customer = order.customer
      return "N/A" unless customer&.ide_user&.user_profile

      begin
        nik = customer.ide_user.nik
        nik.present? ? " #{nik}" : "N/A"
      rescue StringEncryption::DecryptionError, StandardError
        "N/A"
      end
    end

    # Safely get MSISDN number as string to prevent scientific notation in Excel
    # @param activation [PostpaidActivation] the activation to get MSISDN from
    # @return [String] MSISDN number or empty string if not available
    def safe_msisdn_number(activation)
      return "" unless activation&.msisdn_number
      " #{activation.msisdn_number}"
    end
  end
end

class PostpaidActivation < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :msisdn
  belongs_to :order_item
  belongs_to :iccid

  default_scope { includes(:msisdn) }

  scope :parent, -> { where(parent: true) }
  scope :children, -> { where(parent: false) }

  delegate :vanity_type, to: :msisdn, prefix: true
  delegate :number, to: :msisdn, prefix: true, allow_nil: true

  validates :iccid, uniqueness: { allow_nil: true, message: "has already been taken" }
  validates :iccid_id, uniqueness: { scope: :order_item_id, message: "is already used in this order" }
  validates :msisdn_id, uniqueness: { scope: :order_item_id, message: "is already used in this order" }

  def msisdn_number
    msisdn&.msisdn
  end

  def msisdn_dealer_id
    msisdn&.dealer_id
  end

  def iccid_number
    iccid&.iccid
  end

  def retry_activation?
    return false unless failed? || processing? || pending?

    # Only allow retry if GoodIssued job has been successful
    order_item.order.good_issued_successful?
  end

  enum :status, {
    created: "created",
    pending: "pending",
    processing: "processing",
    activated: "activated",
    delivered: "delivered",
    failed: "failed",
    cancelled: "cancelled"
  }
end

class Admin::OrdersController < ApplicationController
  before_action :authenticate_portal_user!
  before_action :authorize_admin
  before_action :set_order, only: [ :show, :edit, :update, :destroy, :retry_good_issued, :consent_letter ]

  # GET /admin/orders
  def index
    authorize Order, policy_class: Admin::OrderPolicy

    @orders = Order
        .exclude_customer_stage
        .where.not(regular_user: nil)
        .filter_and_sort(
          query: params[:q],
          status: params[:status],
          sort_column: sort_column_param,
          sort_direction: sort_direction_param,
          page: params[:page]
        ).includes(
          :location,
          :regular_user,
          :npwp_attachment,
          :akta_attachment,
          :nib_attachment,
          :ktp_owner_attachment,
          :ktp_pic_attachment,
          :account_statement_attachment,
          :power_of_attorney_attachment,
          :mou_attachment)
  end

  # GET /admin/orders/:id
  def show
    authorize @order, policy_class: Admin::OrderPolicy

    @order_items = @order.order_items.includes(:product)
  end

  # GET /admin/orders/new
  def new
    authorize @order, policy_class: Admin::OrderPolicy

    @order = Order.new
  end

  # POST /admin/orders
  def create
    authorize @order, policy_class: Admin::OrderPolicy

    @order = Order.new(order_params)

    if @order.save
      redirect_to portal_admin_order_path(@order), notice: "Order was successfully created."
    else
      flash.now[:alert] = @order.errors.full_messages.first || "Failed to create order."
      render :new, status: :unprocessable_entity
    end
  end

  # GET /admin/orders/:id/edit
  def edit
    authorize @order, policy_class: Admin::OrderPolicy
  end

  # PATCH/PUT /admin/orders/:id
  def update
    authorize @order, policy_class: Admin::OrderPolicy

    if @order.update(order_params)
      redirect_to portal_admin_order_path(@order), notice: "Order was successfully updated."
    else
      flash.now[:alert] = @order.errors.full_messages.first
      render :edit, status: :unprocessable_entity
    end
  end

  # DELETE /admin/orders/:id
  def destroy
    authorize @order, policy_class: Admin::OrderPolicy

    if @order.destroy
      redirect_to portal_admin_orders_path, notice: "Order was successfully deleted."
    else
      redirect_to portal_admin_orders_path, alert: "Failed to delete order."
    end
  end

  # POST /admin/orders/:id/retry_good_issued
  def retry_good_issued
    authorize @order, policy_class: Admin::OrderPolicy

    GoodIssuedJob.perform_later(@order.id)
    redirect_to portal_admin_order_path(@order), notice: "Good Issued API has been queued for retry."
  rescue StandardError => e
    Rails.logger.error "Failed to retry Good Issued for order #{@order.id}: #{e.message}"
    redirect_to portal_admin_order_path(@order), alert: "Failed to retry Good Issued API."
  end

  # GET /admin/orders/:id/consent_letter.pdf
  def consent_letter
    @customer = @order.customer
    @customer_name = @customer&.receiver_name || "Unknown Customer"
    @approval_date = @order.consent_approved_at || Time.current

    respond_to do |format|
      format.pdf do
        pdf_content = WickedPdf.new.pdf_from_string(
          render_to_string(
            template: "customers/email_attachments/consent_letter",
            layout: "pdf",
            formats: [ :html ]
          ),
          encoding: "UTF-8"
        )

        date_str = @approval_date.strftime("%Y%m%d")
        filename = "consent_letter_#{@order.order_reference_number}_#{date_str}.pdf"

        send_data pdf_content,
          filename: filename,
          type: "application/pdf",
          disposition: "inline"
      end
    end
  end

  # GET /portal/admin/orders/export_xls
  def export_xls
    authorize @order, policy_class: Admin::OrderPolicy

    @orders = Order.where.not(regular_user: nil)
      .includes(
        :location,
        :regular_user,
        :npwp_attachment,
        :akta_attachment,
        :nib_attachment,
        :ktp_owner_attachment,
        :ktp_pic_attachment,
        :account_statement_attachment,
        :power_of_attorney_attachment,
        :mou_attachment)


    if params[:q].present?
      search_term = "%#{params[:q]}%"
      @orders = @orders.where(
        "receiver_name LIKE ? OR receiver_email LIKE ? OR receiver_contact_number LIKE ? OR company_name LIKE ?",
        search_term, search_term, search_term, search_term
      )
    end

    if params[:status].present?
      @orders = @orders.where(status: params[:status])
    end

    sort_column = sort_column_param || "created_at"
    sort_direction = sort_direction_param || "desc"
    @orders = @orders.order("#{sort_column} #{sort_direction}")



    excel_data = Export::OrderExportService.new(@orders).generate

    # Set headers for file download
    response.headers["Content-Disposition"] = "attachment; filename=orders_#{Time.current.strftime('%Y%m%d_%H%M%S')}.xlsx"
    response.headers["Content-Type"] = "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet"

    # Return the Excel data
    render plain: excel_data
  end

  private

  # Sets @order with appropriate eager loading based on the current action
  def set_order
    @order = if action_name == "show"
              Order.includes(:sales, :location)
    else
              Order
    end.find(params[:id])
  end

  # Only allow a list of trusted parameters through
  def order_params
    params.require(:order).permit(
      :sales_id,
      :customer_id,
      :location_id,
      :total_price,
      :delivery_price,
      :tax,
      :tax_price,
      :discount_price,
      :status
    )
  end

  # Determine the column to sort by, with validation to prevent SQL injection
  def sort_column_param
    allowed_columns = %w[id total_price status created_at]
    params[:sort].present? && allowed_columns.include?(params[:sort]) ? params[:sort] : nil
  end

  # Determine the sort direction, limited to 'asc' or 'desc' to prevent SQL injection
  def sort_direction_param
    %w[asc desc].include?(params[:direction]) ? params[:direction] : "asc"
  end
end

# ISB-2993: Add MSISDN Count Column to Order Export Report

## Issue Summary
**Title:** Create no of MSSIDN on Download Report form Kelola Pesanan
**Type:** Task
**Status:** To Do
**Priority:** Medium
**Assignee:** Hanif Widiyanto
**Reporter:** Rio Radityo
**Sprint:** ISB Sprint 55

---

## Current Issue Description
Please fill column SIM card with no of MSISDN orders on downloaded Excel from Kelola Report as Admin

**Current Behavior:**
The "SIM CARD" column in the order export Excel shows only the first MSISDN number from the order's postpaid activations. For orders with multiple MSISDNs (bulk orders), the current implementation only displays one MSISDN number, making it impossible to see the total count of MSISDNs in an order.

---

## 1. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (Product Owner Perspective)

### User Story
**As an** Admin user
**I want to** see the total count of MSISDN numbers for each order in the Excel export
**So that** I can quickly understand order size and track bulk order volumes without opening individual orders

### Given-When-Then Scenarios

#### AC-1: Single MSISDN Order Display
**Given** an order has exactly 1 postpaid activation with 1 MSISDN
**When** the admin downloads the order report as Excel
**Then** the "SIM CARD" column should display "1" (the count)
**And** the format should be consistent with other numeric columns

#### AC-2: Multiple MSISDN Order Display (Bulk Orders)
**Given** an order has multiple postpaid activations (e.g., 5 MSISDNs)
**When** the admin downloads the order report as Excel
**Then** the "SIM CARD" column should display "5" (the total count)
**And** the count should include all postpaid activations associated with the order

#### AC-3: Order Without MSISDN Display
**Given** an order has no postpaid activations assigned yet
**When** the admin downloads the order report as Excel
**Then** the "SIM CARD" column should display "0" or "-"
**And** the cell should not be empty

#### AC-4: Excel Formatting
**Given** the Excel file is generated with MSISDN counts
**When** the file is opened in Excel or Google Sheets
**Then** the "SIM CARD" column should be formatted as a number (not text)
**And** the column should support sorting and filtering as numeric data
**And** the column should be right-aligned for better readability

#### AC-5: Filtered Export Consistency
**Given** the admin applies filters (search, status, sort) before exporting
**When** the Excel report is generated
**Then** the "SIM CARD" column counts should match the filtered order data
**And** all filtered orders should have accurate MSISDN counts

#### AC-6: Column Header Update
**Given** the Excel export is generated
**When** viewing the Excel file
**Then** the column header should be renamed from "SIM CARD" to "NO OF MSISDN" or "MSISDN COUNT"
**And** the header should be clear and professional in both English and Indonesian

### Functional Requirements

1. **MSISDN Count Calculation**
   - Count all postpaid activations associated with each order through order_items
   - Include both parent and child postpaid activations in the count
   - Handle orders with zero activations gracefully

2. **Column Positioning**
   - The "NO OF MSISDN" column should remain in the same position (column 7)
   - Maintain consistent column ordering with existing export structure

3. **Data Format**
   - Export as numeric value (integer)
   - Support Excel numeric operations (SUM, AVERAGE, etc.)
   - Right-align for consistency with numeric data

4. **Performance**
   - Maintain existing query performance with eager loading
   - Add necessary includes to prevent N+1 queries
   - Handle large datasets (1000+ orders) efficiently

5. **Bilingual Support**
   - Update column header in both Indonesian and English locale files
   - Suggested translations:
     - English: "NO OF MSISDN" or "MSISDN COUNT"
     - Indonesian: "JUMLAH MSISDN" or "JML NOMOR"

### Non-Functional Requirements

1. **Performance:** Export generation should complete within 30 seconds for 1000 orders
2. **Compatibility:** Excel file should open correctly in Excel 2016+, Google Sheets, and LibreOffice
3. **Data Accuracy:** MSISDN counts must be 100% accurate across all order types
4. **Scalability:** Solution should handle orders with up to 100 MSISDNs per order
5. **Maintainability:** Code should follow existing service patterns in the codebase

### Business Rules and Constraints

1. Only postpaid activations with valid MSISDN associations should be counted
2. Cancelled or deleted postpaid activations should not be included in the count
3. The count should reflect the current state at export time, not historical data
4. Orders in "customer_stage" status should not be included in the export (existing behavior)

### Error Handling and Edge Cases

| Scenario | Expected Behavior |
|----------|-------------------|
| Order with null postpaid_activations | Display "0" |
| Order with soft-deleted activations | Exclude from count |
| Order with mixed parent/child activations | Count all activations |
| Database query timeout | Return error with retry option |
| Empty result set | Generate Excel with headers only |
| Invalid order data | Skip invalid records, log error |

### UX/UI Considerations

1. **Column Header:** Use clear, concise header text
2. **Number Formatting:** Right-align numeric values
3. **Column Width:** Auto-fit column width to accommodate counts up to 3 digits
4. **Consistency:** Match styling with other numeric columns (HARGA TOTAL, DEPOSIT JAMINAN)

### Definition of Done

- [ ] MSISDN count column displays accurate count for all order types
- [ ] Excel file formatting is correct (numeric, right-aligned)
- [ ] Column header updated in both EN and ID locales
- [ ] Unit tests pass with 100% coverage for new/modified code
- [ ] Integration tests verify Excel generation with various scenarios
- [ ] Code reviewed and approved by senior developer
- [ ] No N+1 query issues introduced
- [ ] Performance benchmarks meet requirements (<30s for 1000 orders)
- [ ] Documentation updated (if needed)
- [ ] QA testing completed successfully
- [ ] Deployed to staging environment and verified
- [ ] Product Owner acceptance received

### Dependencies and Risks

**Dependencies:**
- Existing Order and PostpaidActivation models
- Export::OrderExportService service
- Admin::OrdersController#export_xls action
- Locale files for translations

**Risks:**
- **Medium Risk:** Performance degradation with large datasets
  - *Mitigation:* Use counter_cache or optimize query with includes
- **Low Risk:** Breaking existing Excel parsing in downstream systems
  - *Mitigation:* Keep column position same, only change content
- **Low Risk:** Translation inconsistency between platforms
  - *Mitigation:* Review with bilingual team member

# ISB-2993: Add MSISDN Count Column to Order Export Report

## Issue Summary
**Title:** Create no of MSSIDN on Download Report form Kelola Pesanan
**Type:** Task
**Status:** To Do
**Priority:** Medium
**Assignee:** Hanif Widiyanto
**Reporter:** Rio Radityo
**Sprint:** ISB Sprint 55

---

## Current Issue Description
Please fill column SIM card with no of MSISDN orders on downloaded Excel from Kelola Report as Admin

**Current Behavior:**
The "SIM CARD" column in the order export Excel shows only the first MSISDN number from the order's postpaid activations. For orders with multiple MSISDNs (bulk orders), the current implementation only displays one MSISDN number, making it impossible to see the total count of MSISDNs in an order.

---

## 1. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (Product Owner Perspective)

### User Story
**As an** Admin user
**I want to** see the total count of MSISDN numbers for each order in the Excel export
**So that** I can quickly understand order size and track bulk order volumes without opening individual orders

### Given-When-Then Scenarios

#### AC-1: Single MSISDN Order Display
**Given** an order has exactly 1 postpaid activation with 1 MSISDN
**When** the admin downloads the order report as Excel
**Then** the "SIM CARD" column should display "1" (the count)
**And** the format should be consistent with other numeric columns

#### AC-2: Multiple MSISDN Order Display (Bulk Orders)
**Given** an order has multiple postpaid activations (e.g., 5 MSISDNs)
**When** the admin downloads the order report as Excel
**Then** the "SIM CARD" column should display "5" (the total count)
**And** the count should include all postpaid activations associated with the order

#### AC-3: Order Without MSISDN Display
**Given** an order has no postpaid activations assigned yet
**When** the admin downloads the order report as Excel
**Then** the "SIM CARD" column should display "0" or "-"
**And** the cell should not be empty

#### AC-4: Excel Formatting
**Given** the Excel file is generated with MSISDN counts
**When** the file is opened in Excel or Google Sheets
**Then** the "SIM CARD" column should be formatted as a number (not text)
**And** the column should support sorting and filtering as numeric data
**And** the column should be right-aligned for better readability

#### AC-5: Filtered Export Consistency
**Given** the admin applies filters (search, status, sort) before exporting
**When** the Excel report is generated
**Then** the "SIM CARD" column counts should match the filtered order data
**And** all filtered orders should have accurate MSISDN counts

#### AC-6: Column Header Update
**Given** the Excel export is generated
**When** viewing the Excel file
**Then** the column header should be renamed from "SIM CARD" to "NO OF MSISDN" or "MSISDN COUNT"
**And** the header should be clear and professional in both English and Indonesian

### Functional Requirements

1. **MSISDN Count Calculation**
   - Count all postpaid activations associated with each order through order_items
   - Include both parent and child postpaid activations in the count
   - Handle orders with zero activations gracefully

2. **Column Positioning**
   - The "NO OF MSISDN" column should remain in the same position (column 7)
   - Maintain consistent column ordering with existing export structure

3. **Data Format**
   - Export as numeric value (integer)
   - Support Excel numeric operations (SUM, AVERAGE, etc.)
   - Right-align for consistency with numeric data

4. **Performance**
   - Maintain existing query performance with eager loading
   - Add necessary includes to prevent N+1 queries
   - Handle large datasets (1000+ orders) efficiently

5. **Bilingual Support**
   - Update column header in both Indonesian and English locale files
   - Suggested translations:
     - English: "NO OF MSISDN" or "MSISDN COUNT"
     - Indonesian: "JUMLAH MSISDN" or "JML NOMOR"

### Non-Functional Requirements

1. **Performance:** Export generation should complete within 30 seconds for 1000 orders
2. **Compatibility:** Excel file should open correctly in Excel 2016+, Google Sheets, and LibreOffice
3. **Data Accuracy:** MSISDN counts must be 100% accurate across all order types
4. **Scalability:** Solution should handle orders with up to 100 MSISDNs per order
5. **Maintainability:** Code should follow existing service patterns in the codebase

### Business Rules and Constraints

1. Only postpaid activations with valid MSISDN associations should be counted
2. Cancelled or deleted postpaid activations should not be included in the count
3. The count should reflect the current state at export time, not historical data
4. Orders in "customer_stage" status should not be included in the export (existing behavior)

### Error Handling and Edge Cases

| Scenario | Expected Behavior |
|----------|-------------------|
| Order with null postpaid_activations | Display "0" |
| Order with soft-deleted activations | Exclude from count |
| Order with mixed parent/child activations | Count all activations |
| Database query timeout | Return error with retry option |
| Empty result set | Generate Excel with headers only |
| Invalid order data | Skip invalid records, log error |

### UX/UI Considerations

1. **Column Header:** Use clear, concise header text
2. **Number Formatting:** Right-align numeric values
3. **Column Width:** Auto-fit column width to accommodate counts up to 3 digits
4. **Consistency:** Match styling with other numeric columns (HARGA TOTAL, DEPOSIT JAMINAN)

### Definition of Done

- [ ] MSISDN count column displays accurate count for all order types
- [ ] Excel file formatting is correct (numeric, right-aligned)
- [ ] Column header updated in both EN and ID locales
- [ ] Unit tests pass with 100% coverage for new/modified code
- [ ] Integration tests verify Excel generation with various scenarios
- [ ] Code reviewed and approved by senior developer
- [ ] No N+1 query issues introduced
- [ ] Performance benchmarks meet requirements (<30s for 1000 orders)
- [ ] Documentation updated (if needed)
- [ ] QA testing completed successfully
- [ ] Deployed to staging environment and verified
- [ ] Product Owner acceptance received

### Dependencies and Risks

**Dependencies:**
- Existing Order and PostpaidActivation models
- Export::OrderExportService service
- Admin::OrdersController#export_xls action
- Locale files for translations

**Risks:**
- **Medium Risk:** Performance degradation with large datasets
  - *Mitigation:* Use counter_cache or optimize query with includes
- **Low Risk:** Breaking existing Excel parsing in downstream systems
  - *Mitigation:* Keep column position same, only change content
- **Low Risk:** Translation inconsistency between platforms
  - *Mitigation:* Review with bilingual team member

## 2. TEST CASES (QA Engineer Perspective)

### Test Case 1: Single MSISDN Order Export
**ID:** TC-ISB-2993-001
**Priority:** High
**Type:** Functional
**Automation:** YES

**Preconditions:**
- User logged in as Admin
- At least one order exists with exactly 1 postpaid activation

**Test Steps:**
1. Navigate to `/portal/admin/orders`
2. Click "Export Excel" button
3. Open the downloaded Excel file
4. Locate an order with 1 MSISDN
5. Check the "NO OF MSISDN" column value

**Expected Result:**
- Column displays "1"
- Value is right-aligned
- Cell format is numeric

**Automation Recommendation:** YES
```javascript

test('should display count of 1 for single MSISDN orders', async ({ page }) => {
  // Setup: Create order with 1 activation
  await createOrderWithActivations(1);

  await page.goto('/portal/admin/orders');
  await page.click('text=Export Excel');

  // Download and parse Excel
  const buffer = await downloadExcelFile(page);
  const workbook = parseExcelBuffer(buffer);
  const sheet = workbook.Sheets['Orders'];

  // Find row for test order
  const msisdnCell = sheet['G2']; // Column G, row 2
  expect(msisdnCell.v).toBe(1);
  expect(msisdnCell.t).toBe('n'); // numeric type
});
```

### Test Case 2: Bulk Order with Multiple MSISDNs

**Priority:** High

**Test Steps:**
